stages.name: Apertura
stages.note: Single round-robin (19 matches), plus an extra regional-derby round in most seasons. Top 8 to two groups of four.

stages.name: Apertura semi-finals
stages.note: Two groups of four, double round-robin; group winners to a two-legged final.

playoff.note: Cuadrangulares: two groups of four play a double round-robin from zero; the two group winners meet in a two-legged final. Two champions per season (Apertura and Finalizacion).

stages.name: Torneo I
stages.note: Single round-robin, 15 or 16 matches (an extra derby round in some seasons). Top 8 to two groups of four.

stages.name: Grand Final
stages.note: Winners of the two tournaments; used only in the scenario where neither is in the top two of the aggregate table.

playoff.note: Two promotions, decided by a conditional set of rules: if one club wins both tournaments it is promoted and the next two in the aggregate table play off; if both winners are top two in the aggregate table both go up; otherwise a grand final plus a play-off against the aggregate table's best remaining club decides the second place.

boundaries.note: Down: the bottom two of the three-season average table (promedio), not the season table, so a bad single season may not relegate a club. Up: exactly two clubs, but only in the simplest scenarios are both decided by the table; in the main scenario one goes up through the grand final and the other through a two-legged play-off, so up_playoff is 1 (at most one place is a play-off).

conflicts.topic: A single row per league, but two championships per season
conflicts.detail: COL1 is stored as one league, but the Colombian top flight runs two independent tournaments (Apertura and Finalizacion), each with its own champion and its own semi-final groups and final. The row name 'Liga Dimayor Finalizacion' names only the second half. Fixtures, form and the title race reset in July.

conflicts.topic: Relegation is not decided by the season table
conflicts.detail: The bottom two are relegated on a three-season average of first-stage points (promedio). A newly promoted club carries only its own seasons in the average, which is why the rule historically protected big clubs.

Since 2025, how the two Primera B promotions are decided depends on where the two short-tournament winners finish in the aggregate table (four scenarios, ranging from both direct to a grand final plus a play-off). The count (2) is fixed; the route is not.
The second tier's infobox has no relegation, and no club drops out of the professional pyramid from it. It is therefore closed downwards even though Primera C exists as an amateur/regional level.

notes: Calendar-year season (2026 Apertura + Finalizacion); the 2026 season is nearly over at the research date. Sizes 20/16 and levels match our rows. Reserve/filial sides historically appear in Primera B (e.g. America B, Nacional B) but none is in the 2026 field and the promotion rules above do not mention them. Cups and CONMEBOL competitions excluded.
